user_goal: Let users pop the exact Plotkeeper surface into their default browser and avoid fixed-port collisions by persisting one private loopback connector shared by every Plotkeeper entry point.

authority.verbatim_text:
Dont suppose you can add a 'pop out into a separate browser window' button can you? Would be nice to see the surface beyond just the codex app itself in the sidebar?

OH ALSO - I wanted to make sure, with PK - we arent assigning some internal IP:port that would be taken up/overlapping by other potential processes right?  If so, can we make it some really obscure connector so that it just generally wouldnt interfere?

baseline.protected_ref: local validated responsive-picker successor of public v0.1.6
baseline.protection_evidence: clean single main worktree; local candidate has independent VALIDATED PASS and is one commit ahead of origin/main
baseline.selection_reason: Current exact source and live dashboard onto which the authorized pop-out and connector behavior must be added.

resources: installed Codex Plotkeeper config and bundled SpecSwarm skill
owned local Plotkeeper listener and Windows default-browser launch path
semantic_changes: Choose an available OS-assigned high dynamic/private loopback port on first install, persist it atomically, and reuse it across reinstall, startup, CLI, service URLs, SpecSwarm health/panel checks, and documentation.
Preserve an explicit user-supplied port override by validating and persisting that connector without taking over foreign listeners.
Add an accessible dashboard button whose loopback-only POST asks Plotkeeper to open the exact current run URL in the Windows default browser.
Reject non-loopback, cross-origin, malformed, missing, stale, or mismatched pop-out requests without launching a browser.

No binding beyond 127.0.0.1, remote browser-launch API, fixed replacement magic port, silent foreign-process termination, port stealing, broad firewall rule, authentication weakening, run identity change, ledger mutation, release, version bump, or GitHub publication.
No arbitrary URL or executable accepted by the pop-out endpoint; it may open only the service's own loopback origin with the request's existing path/query locator.
No loss of existing explicit -Port/--port support or migration break for the currently installed 47831 connector.

invariants: Plotkeeper binds only to 127.0.0.1 and never stops a listener it cannot prove it owns.
One valid connector record is the source of truth for every automatically constructed Plotkeeper URL and startup command.
Existing installations retain their healthy owned connector during upgrade; new installations avoid a fixed default and reuse their persisted connector.
Pop-out opens the exact current pathname and query on the same connector, never an arbitrary URL, and reports success or failure truthfully.
Run enrollment, active filtering, successor history, review/check-in behavior, responsive picker behavior, and ledger data remain unchanged.

acceptance_cases.promised_behavior: The Pop out button launches the exact bound Plotkeeper URL in the Windows default browser from the sidebar surface.
acceptance_cases.forbidden_behavior: It opens only another embedded panel, drops the run locator, launches an arbitrary URL, or claims success without a browser-launch call.
acceptance_cases.target_and_actor: A user viewing a run-bound Plotkeeper dashboard in Codex.

acceptance_cases.promised_behavior: A new install chooses and persists one available high private loopback port and every automatic entry point uses it across restart/reinstall.
acceptance_cases.forbidden_behavior: A fixed default collides, entry points disagree, or the connector changes on routine restart/reinstall.
acceptance_cases.target_and_actor: Plotkeeper installer, startup, CLI, service, SpecSwarm, and dashboard URL generation.

acceptance_cases.promised_behavior: Foreign listeners and invalid connector records fail closed without process termination, fallback takeover, or browser launch.
acceptance_cases.forbidden_behavior: Plotkeeper kills, replaces, binds over, or silently bypasses a foreign listener or malformed connector.
acceptance_cases.target_and_actor: Installer/startup and pop-out endpoint under adversarial local conditions.

proof_requirements.claim: A real loopback request from the live dashboard calls a captured default-browser launcher exactly once with the exact same-origin run-bound URL, while adversarial origins/URLs launch zero times.
proof_requirements.required_environment: isolated server plus live local browser
proof_requirements.command_or_read_only_check: backend route tests and browser interaction with exact URL/response assertions
proof_requirements.expected_observation: one truthful launch and visible success state; invalid requests fail with no launch

proof_requirements.claim: Fresh isolated install, restart, and reinstall use one persisted OS-assigned port in the dynamic/private range across connector JSON, startup registration, CLI URLs, service health, and installed SpecSwarm instructions.
proof_requirements.required_environment: isolated Z-drive installation and Codex home
proof_requirements.command_or_read_only_check: real install/reinstall harness with connector and byte-parity assertions
proof_requirements.expected_observation: same available high port everywhere and healthy exact dashboard after each lifecycle step

proof_requirements.claim: A real foreign listener remains the same PID/content and startup/install exits nonzero; malformed connector and cross-origin pop-out attacks are rejected.
proof_requirements.required_environment: isolated ports, connector files, and disposable server
proof_requirements.command_or_read_only_check: foreign-listener, malformed-record, origin, host, and arbitrary-path adversarial fixtures
proof_requirements.expected_observation: foreign process survives unchanged and every invalid path fails closed

review_requirements.required_role: independent security and lifecycle reviewer of connector selection, ownership, origin checks, and browser launch

release_requirements.required_receipt: validated local implementation and installed-live proof; publication requires a separate release contract

stop_conditions: Unexpected diff, non-loopback bind, arbitrary browser URL, origin bypass, port disagreement, foreign process mutation, unstable reinstall connector, stale sidebar URL, failed lifecycle/full/browser test, dirty candidate, or ledger/project-repository mutation.
known_discrepancies: The current installed connector is fixed at 127.0.0.1:47831; ownership checks prevent takeover but a foreign listener can block startup.
SpecSwarm health and surface checks currently hardcode 47831 even though run dashboard URLs are already stored per run.
The dashboard has no host-side mechanism to ask Windows to open the exact current surface in the default external browser.
Local main includes the independently validated responsive-picker commit 58f3dee and is one commit ahead of public main.
